chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and he was the in-law of Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said:

Bureyd said to Muhammad, 'Ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for me about something I intend to do. Indeed, people have deposits and wealth in my hand, and I am moving about in them, and I have intended to withdraw from the world and to give to each one with a right his right.'

He said, so Muhammad asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that and informed him of the story and said, 'What do you see for him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Does he begin with himself by paying the debt? No! But he should take and give, upon Allah, Majestic is His Name.'

key_terms.أَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهَا: moving about in them (managing/using the wealth)
key_terms.وَدَائِعَ: deposits or trusts held for others

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on settling financial deposits and debts before withdrawing from worldly life?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for active engagement in commerce over premature asceticism, provided one fulfills trusts (amanat). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Bureyd to maintain his business activities to settle debts, illustrating that worldly duties are a form of worship when executed with divine consciousness. This reflects the broader scholarly view that financial responsibility is a prerequisite for spiritual retreat, ensuring no rights are neglected.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, and he was the in-law of Bureyd Al Ijaly.

Bureyd said to Muhammad, ‘Ask Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> for me about something. I want to do such that the deposits and the wealth which I hold for the people, and I keep turning in these, and I have intended that I shall empty myself from the world and hand over to each one with his right, (from the) rights (I have with me)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Muhammad asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that, and informed him<sup>asws</sup> of the story and said, ‘What do you<sup>asws</sup> see for him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad! Has he initiated the war against himself. No! But, he should take and give, upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Name’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah al-Hajjal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Burayd al-Tjliy wanted to get married. Burayd said, to Muhammad, ‘Ask abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, about what I am planning to do. I want to return people’s properties left with me for safe- keeping and it keeps me involved. Thereafter I like to stay away from the worldly things and return everyone’s things that belong to them.

He (the narrator) has said, ‘Muhammad asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it, informed him of the story and asked about his decision.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Does he want to start a fight against his own soul? He must not do so. Instead, he must give and take for the sake of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
